title: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
description: All 18 CIS Controls and their 153 Safeguards as defences set to todo, under the attacks they defend against. The 56 Implementation Group 1 safeguards — the essential cyber hygiene every enterprise should have — say so in their description; start there. Safeguard titles follow the CIS publication; descriptions are summaries, not the CIS text.

risks.title: Ransomware or destructive attack on the enterprise
risks.description: An attacker encrypts or destroys systems and data across the enterprise, halting operations and forcing a choice between paying and rebuilding.

risks.title: Theft or exposure of sensitive data
risks.description: Sensitive enterprise or customer data is copied out by an attacker, exposed through a misconfiguration, or leaked by an insider or service provider.

risks.title: Disruption of enterprise operations
risks.description: Systems the enterprise runs on become unavailable through attack, failure or a compromised provider, and recovery takes longer than the business can tolerate.

attacks.title: Unmanaged or unknown assets and software exploited
attacks.description: Devices and software nobody inventoried — shadow IT, forgotten servers, unsupported applications — are unpatched and unmonitored, and an attacker finds them first.

attacks.title: Phishing and social engineering
attacks.description: A convincing email, message or call leads someone to open a malicious file, visit a malicious site or hand over credentials.

attacks.title: Malware and ransomware execution
attacks.description: Malicious code runs on an endpoint or server, from an attachment, a download, removable media or an exploited service.

attacks.title: Exploitation of vulnerabilities and insecure configuration
attacks.description: Known vulnerabilities, default settings, unnecessary services or open ports on enterprise assets are exploited.

attacks.title: Credential theft and account abuse
attacks.description: Stolen, guessed, reused or default credentials — and dormant or over-privileged accounts — give an attacker legitimate-looking access.

attacks.title: Network intrusion and lateral movement
attacks.description: Once inside, an attacker moves across a flat or poorly monitored network towards high-value systems and administrative access.

attacks.title: Sensitive data exposed or exfiltrated
attacks.description: Data that is not inventoried, classified, access-controlled and encrypted leaks through misconfigured shares, lost devices, removable media or exfiltration.

attacks.title: Attack on in-house or acquired application software
attacks.description: Flaws in applications the enterprise develops, buys or integrates — injection, broken access control, vulnerable components — are exploited.

attacks.title: Compromise through a service provider
attacks.description: A provider holding enterprise data or access to enterprise systems is breached, fails, or is not held to security requirements.

attacks.title: Insider misuse of access
attacks.description: An employee or contractor uses access they hold — or should no longer hold — to take or damage data.

attacks.title: Attacker activity goes undetected
attacks.description: Logs are not collected, reviewed or retained, alerts are not tuned and incidents have no process, so an intrusion runs for weeks before anyone notices.

attacks.title: Recovery fails when it is needed
attacks.description: Backups are missing, incomplete, reachable by the attacker or never tested, so the enterprise cannot restore after an incident.

defences.title: 1.1 Establish and Maintain Detailed Enterprise Asset Inventory
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. An accurate, detailed inventory of every enterprise asset that stores or processes data — end-user devices, servers, network and IoT devices, including remote and cloud — reviewed at least twice a year.

defences.title: 1.2 Address Unauthorized Assets
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A process to deal with unauthorized assets weekly: remove, deny network access or quarantine them.

defences.title: 1.3 Utilize an Active Discovery Tool
defences.description: An active discovery tool identifies assets connected to the network, run at least daily, feeding the inventory.

defences.title: 1.4 Use Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Logging to Update Enterprise Asset Inventory
defences.description: DHCP logging on servers or IP address management tools is used to update the asset inventory at least weekly.

defences.title: 1.5 Use a Passive Asset Discovery Tool
defences.description: A passive discovery tool identifies assets from network traffic, reviewed at least weekly.

defences.title: 2.1 Establish and Maintain a Software Inventory
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A detailed inventory of all licensed software installed on enterprise assets — title, publisher, version, purpose — reviewed twice a year.

defences.title: 2.2 Ensure Authorized Software is Currently Supported
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Only software still supported by its vendor is authorized; unsupported software is documented as an exception with mitigating controls, or removed.

defences.title: 2.3 Address Unauthorized Software
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Unauthorized software is removed or documented as an exception, reviewed at least monthly.

defences.title: 2.4 Utilize Automated Software Inventory Tools
defences.description: Software inventory tools automate the discovery and documentation of installed software.

defences.title: 2.5 Allowlist Authorized Software
defences.description: Technical controls such as application allowlisting ensure only authorized software can execute or be accessed.

defences.title: 2.6 Allowlist Authorized Libraries
defences.description: Only authorized software libraries — specific .dll, .ocx, .so files — are allowed to load into a system process.

defences.title: 2.7 Allowlist Authorized Scripts
defences.description: Only authorized, digitally signed scripts such as .ps1 and .py are allowed to execute.

defences.title: 3.1 Establish and Maintain a Data Management Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented data management process covering data sensitivity, ownership, handling, retention limits and disposal, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 3.2 Establish and Maintain a Data Inventory
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. An inventory of sensitive data, based on the data management process, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 3.3 Configure Data Access Control Lists
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Access control lists restrict access to data on local and remote file systems, databases and applications according to need to know.

defences.title: 3.4 Enforce Data Retention
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Data is retained for the minimum and no longer than the maximum timelines in the data management process.

defences.title: 3.5 Securely Dispose of Data
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Data is disposed of securely, with methods matched to its sensitivity.

defences.title: 3.6 Encrypt Data on End-User Devices
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Data on end-user devices holding sensitive data is encrypted — full-disk or equivalent.

defences.title: 3.7 Establish and Maintain a Data Classification Scheme
defences.description: A classification scheme — such as sensitive, confidential, public — is applied to data in the inventory and reviewed annually.

defences.title: 3.8 Document Data Flows
defences.description: Data flows, including those with service providers, are documented and reviewed annually.

defences.title: 3.9 Encrypt Data on Removable Media
defences.description: Data on removable media is encrypted.

defences.title: 3.10 Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit
defences.description: Sensitive data is encrypted in transit, for example with TLS or OpenSSH.

defences.title: 3.11 Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
defences.description: Sensitive data is encrypted at rest on servers, applications and databases.

defences.title: 3.12 Segment Data Processing and Storage Based on Sensitivity
defences.description: Data processing and storage are segmented by sensitivity, so less sensitive systems do not hold or reach more sensitive data.

defences.title: 3.13 Deploy a Data Loss Prevention Solution
defences.description: An automated tool such as host-based data loss prevention identifies sensitive data and its movement.

defences.title: 3.14 Log Sensitive Data Access
defences.description: Access to sensitive data — including modification and disposal — is logged.

defences.title: 4.1 Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented secure configuration process for enterprise assets and software, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 4.2 Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process for Network Infrastructure
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented secure configuration process for network devices, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 4.3 Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Sessions lock automatically after a defined period of inactivity — at most 15 minutes on general-purpose systems and 2 minutes on mobile devices.

defences.title: 4.4 Implement and Manage a Firewall on Servers
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Servers run a firewall, or one is provided in front of them.

defences.title: 4.5 Implement and Manage a Firewall on End-User Devices
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. End-user devices run a host-based firewall with a default-deny rule for everything not explicitly allowed.

defences.title: 4.6 Securely Manage Enterprise Assets and Software
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Assets and software are managed securely — version-controlled infrastructure-as-code, secure protocols such as SSH and HTTPS for administration.

defences.title: 4.7 Manage Default Accounts on Enterprise Assets and Software
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Default accounts — root, administrator, pre-configured vendor accounts — are disabled or made unusable.

defences.title: 4.8 Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
defences.description: Unnecessary services — unused file-sharing, web application modules, service functions — are uninstalled or disabled.

defences.title: 4.9 Configure Trusted DNS Servers on Enterprise Assets
defences.description: Assets use enterprise-controlled or reputable externally accessible DNS servers.

defences.title: 4.10 Enforce Automatic Device Lockout on Portable End-User Devices
defences.description: Portable devices lock out after a set number of failed local authentication attempts.

defences.title: 4.11 Enforce Remote Wipe Capability on Portable End-User Devices
defences.description: Portable devices can be wiped remotely when lost or stolen, or when someone leaves.

defences.title: 4.12 Separate Enterprise Workspaces on Mobile End-User Devices
defences.description: Mobile devices keep enterprise applications and data in a separate workspace.

defences.title: 5.1 Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Accounts
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. An inventory of all accounts — user and administrator — with name, username, start and stop dates and department, validated quarterly.

defences.title: 5.2 Use Unique Passwords
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Unique passwords for every asset — at least 8 characters with MFA, 14 without.

defences.title: 5.3 Disable Dormant Accounts
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Accounts inactive for 45 days are deleted or disabled.

defences.title: 5.4 Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Administrator Accounts
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Administrator privileges sit on dedicated administrator accounts, and day-to-day work uses non-privileged accounts.

defences.title: 5.5 Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Accounts
defences.description: An inventory of service accounts — department owner, review date, purpose — validated quarterly.

defences.title: 5.6 Centralize Account Management
defences.description: Accounts are managed centrally through a directory or identity service.

defences.title: 6.1 Establish an Access Granting Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A process, preferably automated, for granting access on new hire, rights grant or role change.

defences.title: 6.2 Establish an Access Revoking Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A process, preferably automated, for revoking access on termination, revocation or role change — disabling accounts rather than deleting them, to keep audit trails.

defences.title: 6.3 Require MFA for Externally-Exposed Applications
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Multi-factor authentication is required for all externally-exposed enterprise and third-party applications.

defences.title: 6.4 Require MFA for Remote Network Access
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Multi-factor authentication is required for remote network access.

defences.title: 6.5 Require MFA for Administrative Access
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrative access, on-site and through service providers.

defences.title: 6.6 Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Authentication and Authorization Systems
defences.description: An inventory of the enterprise's authentication and authorization systems, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 6.7 Centralize Access Control
defences.description: Access control for all assets is centralized through a directory service or SSO provider.

defences.title: 6.8 Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control
defences.description: Role-based access control: the rights each role needs are documented and access is reviewed at least annually.

defences.title: 7.1 Establish and Maintain a Vulnerability Management Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented vulnerability management process for enterprise assets, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 7.2 Establish and Maintain a Remediation Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A risk-based remediation strategy with monthly or more frequent reviews.

defences.title: 7.3 Perform Automated Operating System Patch Management
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Operating system updates are applied automatically on a monthly or more frequent basis.

defences.title: 7.4 Perform Automated Application Patch Management
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Application updates are applied automatically on a monthly or more frequent basis.

defences.title: 7.5 Perform Automated Vulnerability Scans of Internal Enterprise Assets
defences.description: Internal assets are scanned for vulnerabilities, authenticated and unauthenticated, quarterly or more often.

defences.title: 7.6 Perform Automated Vulnerability Scans of Externally-Exposed Enterprise Assets
defences.description: Externally-exposed assets are scanned for vulnerabilities monthly or more often.

defences.title: 7.7 Remediate Detected Vulnerabilities
defences.description: Detected vulnerabilities are remediated through tools and processes monthly or more often, based on the remediation process.

defences.title: 8.1 Establish and Maintain an Audit Log Management Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented process defining logging requirements — collection, review, retention — reviewed annually.

defences.title: 8.2 Collect Audit Logs
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Audit logging is enabled across enterprise assets as the log management process defines.

defences.title: 8.3 Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Logging destinations have enough storage to meet the log management process.

defences.title: 8.4 Standardize Time Synchronization
defences.description: Time is synchronized across assets from at least two synchronized time sources.

defences.title: 8.5 Collect Detailed Audit Logs
defences.description: Detailed logs are collected for assets with sensitive data — event source, date, username, timestamp, source and destination addresses.

defences.title: 8.6 Collect DNS Query Audit Logs
defences.description: DNS query logs are collected where appropriate and supported.

defences.title: 8.7 Collect URL Request Audit Logs
defences.description: URL request logs are collected where appropriate and supported.

defences.title: 8.8 Collect Command-Line Audit Logs
defences.description: Command-line logs — PowerShell, BASH, remote administrative terminals — are collected.

defences.title: 8.9 Centralize Audit Logs
defences.description: Audit logs are centralized, to the extent possible, for collection and retention.

defences.title: 8.10 Retain Audit Logs
defences.description: Audit logs are retained for at least 90 days.

defences.title: 8.11 Conduct Audit Log Reviews
defences.description: Audit logs are reviewed weekly or more often to detect anomalies or abnormal events that could indicate a threat.

defences.title: 8.12 Collect Service Provider Logs
defences.description: Service provider logs are collected where supported — authentication, data modification and user management events.

defences.title: 9.1 Ensure Use of Only Fully Supported Browsers and Email Clients
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Only fully supported browsers and email clients, at the latest vendor version, are allowed to run.

defences.title: 9.2 Use DNS Filtering Services
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. DNS filtering services block access to known malicious domains on all assets.

defences.title: 9.3 Maintain and Enforce Network-Based URL Filters
defences.description: Network-based URL filters limit access to potentially malicious or unapproved websites.

defences.title: 9.4 Restrict Unnecessary or Unauthorized Browser and Email Client Extensions
defences.description: Unauthorized or unnecessary browser and email client plugins, extensions and add-ons are restricted by uninstalling or disabling them.

defences.title: 9.5 Implement DMARC
defences.description: DMARC, with SPF and DKIM, lowers the chance of spoofed or modified emails from valid domains.

defences.title: 9.6 Block Unnecessary File Types
defences.description: Unnecessary file types attempting to enter the email gateway are blocked.

defences.title: 9.7 Deploy and Maintain Email Server Anti-Malware Protections
defences.description: Email server anti-malware protections — attachment scanning, sandboxing — are deployed and maintained.

defences.title: 10.1 Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Anti-malware software runs on all enterprise assets.

defences.title: 10.2 Configure Automatic Anti-Malware Signature Updates
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Anti-malware signature files update automatically on all assets.

defences.title: 10.3 Disable Autorun and Autoplay for Removable Media
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Autorun and autoplay are disabled for removable media.

defences.title: 10.4 Configure Automatic Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Media
defences.description: Removable media is scanned for malware automatically.

defences.title: 10.5 Enable Anti-Exploitation Features
defences.description: Anti-exploitation features — data execution prevention, exploit protection, System Integrity Protection — are enabled where possible.

defences.title: 10.6 Centrally Manage Anti-Malware Software
defences.description: Anti-malware software is managed centrally.

defences.title: 10.7 Use Behavior-Based Anti-Malware Software
defences.description: Behaviour-based anti-malware software is used, to catch what signatures miss.

defences.title: 11.1 Establish and Maintain a Data Recovery Process
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented data recovery process — scope, prioritisation, backup security — reviewed annually.

defences.title: 11.2 Perform Automated Backups
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. In-scope assets are backed up automatically, weekly or more often depending on data sensitivity.

defences.title: 11.3 Protect Recovery Data
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Recovery data is protected with the same controls as the original data — encryption, separation.

defences.title: 11.4 Establish and Maintain an Isolated Instance of Recovery Data
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. An isolated instance of recovery data — offline, cloud or off-site, version-controlled — out of an attacker's reach.

defences.title: 11.5 Test Data Recovery
defences.description: Backup recovery is tested quarterly or more often for a sample of in-scope assets.

defences.title: 12.1 Ensure Network Infrastructure is Up-to-Date
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Network infrastructure runs the latest stable release of software and supported network-as-a-service offerings, reviewed monthly.

defences.title: 12.2 Establish and Maintain a Secure Network Architecture
defences.description: A secure network architecture — segmentation, least privilege, availability — documented and reviewed annually.

defences.title: 12.3 Securely Manage Network Infrastructure
defences.description: Network infrastructure is managed securely — version-controlled infrastructure-as-code, secure protocols.

defences.title: 12.4 Establish and Maintain Architecture Diagram(s)
defences.description: Architecture diagrams and other network system documentation, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 12.5 Centralize Network Authentication, Authorization, and Auditing (AAA)
defences.description: Network authentication, authorization and auditing are centralized.

defences.title: 12.6 Use of Secure Network Management and Communication Protocols
defences.description: Secure network management and communication protocols such as 802.1X and WPA2 Enterprise or better are used.

defences.title: 12.7 Ensure Remote Devices Utilize a VPN and are Connecting to an Enterprise's AAA Infrastructure
defences.description: Remote users connect through a VPN and the enterprise's authentication infrastructure before accessing enterprise resources.

defences.title: 12.8 Establish and Maintain Dedicated Computing Resources for All Administrative Work
defences.description: Administrative work is done on dedicated, segmented computing resources with no internet access for general use.

defences.title: 13.1 Centralize Security Event Alerting
defences.description: Security event alerting is centralized — a SIEM or log analytics platform with correlation and alerting.

defences.title: 13.2 Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Detection Solution
defences.description: Host-based intrusion detection runs on assets where appropriate and supported.

defences.title: 13.3 Deploy a Network Intrusion Detection Solution
defences.description: Network intrusion detection runs on enterprise assets where appropriate.

defences.title: 13.4 Perform Traffic Filtering Between Network Segments
defences.description: Traffic between network segments is filtered where appropriate.

defences.title: 13.5 Manage Access Control for Remote Assets
defences.description: Remote assets are checked before connecting — up-to-date anti-malware, configuration compliance, patched operating system and applications.

defences.title: 13.6 Collect Network Traffic Flow Logs
defences.description: Network traffic flow logs are collected and reviewed for alerts.

defences.title: 13.7 Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Prevention Solution
defences.description: Host-based intrusion prevention — an EDR client or host-based IPS agent — runs where appropriate.

defences.title: 13.8 Deploy a Network Intrusion Prevention Solution
defences.description: Network intrusion prevention runs where appropriate.

defences.title: 13.9 Deploy Port-Level Access Control
defences.description: Port-level access control — 802.1x or similar — with user and device authentication.

defences.title: 13.10 Perform Application Layer Filtering
defences.description: Application layer filtering through a filtering proxy, application firewall or gateway.

defences.title: 13.11 Tune Security Event Alerting Thresholds
defences.description: Alerting thresholds are tuned monthly or more often, so real alerts are not lost in noise.

defences.title: 14.1 Establish and Maintain a Security Awareness Program
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A security awareness programme, run at hire and at least annually, reviewed and updated annually.

defences.title: 14.2 Train Workforce Members to Recognize Social Engineering Attacks
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. The workforce is trained to recognise phishing, business email compromise, pretexting and tailgating.

defences.title: 14.3 Train Workforce Members on Authentication Best Practices
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Training on authentication — MFA, password composition, credential management.

defences.title: 14.4 Train Workforce on Data Handling Best Practices
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Training on identifying, storing, transferring, archiving and destroying sensitive data, including clear desk and clear screen.

defences.title: 14.5 Train Workforce Members on Causes of Unintentional Data Exposure
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Training on how data is exposed by accident — mis-delivery, lost devices, publishing to unintended audiences.

defences.title: 14.6 Train Workforce Members on Recognizing and Reporting Security Incidents
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. The workforce can recognise a potential incident and knows how to report it.

defences.title: 14.7 Train Workforce on How to Identify and Report if Their Enterprise Assets are Missing Security Updates
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. The workforce can tell when their devices are missing updates and knows how to report it.

defences.title: 14.8 Train Workforce on the Dangers of Connecting to and Transmitting Enterprise Data Over Insecure Networks
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Training on the dangers of insecure networks for enterprise work, including home network configuration for remote workers.

defences.title: 14.9 Conduct Role-Specific Security Awareness and Skills Training
defences.description: Role-specific training — secure configuration for IT staff, OWASP Top 10 for developers, advanced social engineering for high-profile roles.

defences.title: 15.1 Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. An inventory of service providers with a classification and an enterprise contact for each, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 15.2 Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy
defences.description: A service provider management policy covering classification, inventory, assessment, monitoring and decommissioning, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 15.3 Classify Service Providers
defences.description: Service providers are classified by data sensitivity, volume, availability requirements, regulations and inherent risk.

defences.title: 15.4 Ensure Service Provider Contracts Include Security Requirements
defences.description: Contracts include security requirements — minimum programme requirements, incident notification, encryption, data disposal.

defences.title: 15.5 Assess Service Providers
defences.description: Service providers are assessed, according to the policy, before onboarding and at renewal — by questionnaire, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report, or other evidence.

defences.title: 15.6 Monitor Service Providers
defences.description: Service providers are monitored — reassessment, release notes, dark web monitoring — according to the policy.

defences.title: 15.7 Securely Decommission Service Providers
defences.description: Service providers are decommissioned securely — user and service accounts deactivated, data flows stopped, enterprise data disposed of.

defences.title: 16.1 Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process
defences.description: A documented secure application development process — secure design, coding, training, vulnerability management, third-party code — reviewed annually.

defences.title: 16.2 Establish and Maintain a Process to Accept and Address Software Vulnerabilities
defences.description: A process to accept and address reports of software vulnerabilities, including a way for external parties to report them.

defences.title: 16.3 Perform Root Cause Analysis on Security Vulnerabilities
defences.description: Root cause analysis on security vulnerabilities, so classes of flaw are fixed rather than individual instances.

defences.title: 16.4 Establish and Manage an Inventory of Third-Party Software Components
defences.description: An inventory of third-party components used in development — a bill of materials — evaluated monthly for risk.

defences.title: 16.5 Use Up-to-Date and Trusted Third-Party Software Components
defences.description: Third-party components come from trusted sources, are evaluated before use, and are kept up to date.

defences.title: 16.6 Establish and Maintain a Severity Rating System and Process for Application Vulnerabilities
defences.description: A severity rating system and process for application vulnerabilities, so fixes are prioritised, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 16.7 Use Standard Hardening Configuration Templates for Application Infrastructure
defences.description: Standard, industry-recommended hardening templates for application infrastructure — servers, databases, web servers, containers, PaaS and SaaS.

defences.title: 16.8 Separate Production and Non-Production Systems
defences.description: Production and non-production environments are kept separate.

defences.title: 16.9 Train Developers in Application Security Concepts and Secure Coding
defences.description: Developers are trained in application security and secure coding, at least annually.

defences.title: 16.10 Apply Secure Design Principles in Application Architectures
defences.description: Secure design principles — least privilege, validation of all inputs, secure defaults, minimal attack surface — applied in application architectures.

defences.title: 16.11 Leverage Vetted Modules or Services for Application Security Components
defences.description: Vetted modules or services are used for identity management, encryption, auditing and logging, instead of building them.

defences.title: 16.12 Implement Code-Level Security Checks
defences.description: Static and dynamic analysis tools check code against secure coding practices during the life cycle.

defences.title: 16.13 Conduct Application Penetration Testing
defences.description: Authenticated application penetration testing for critical applications, to find business logic flaws scanners miss.

defences.title: 16.14 Conduct Threat Modeling
defences.description: Threat modelling identifies and addresses application design flaws before code is written.

defences.title: 17.1 Designate Personnel to Manage Incident Handling
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. One key person, and at least one backup, manage the incident handling process.

defences.title: 17.2 Establish and Maintain Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. Contact information for parties who need to be told of incidents — internal staff, service providers, law enforcement, insurers, government — kept current.

defences.title: 17.3 Establish and Maintain an Enterprise Process for Reporting Incidents
defences.description: IG1 — essential cyber hygiene. A documented process for the workforce to report security incidents — timeframe, recipients, mechanism, minimum information.

defences.title: 17.4 Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process
defences.description: A documented incident response process covering roles, compliance reporting and a communication plan, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 17.5 Assign Key Roles and Responsibilities
defences.description: Key incident response roles — legal, IT, security, facilities, public relations, HR, incident responders, analysts — assigned.

defences.title: 17.6 Define Mechanisms for Communicating During Incident Response
defences.description: Primary and secondary communication mechanisms for incident response, so the team can still talk if normal channels are compromised.

defences.title: 17.7 Conduct Routine Incident Response Exercises
defences.description: Routine incident response exercises and scenarios, at least annually.

defences.title: 17.8 Conduct Post-Incident Reviews
defences.description: Post-incident reviews identify lessons learned and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.

defences.title: 17.9 Establish and Maintain Security Incident Thresholds
defences.description: Thresholds that distinguish an incident from an event, reviewed annually.

defences.title: 18.1 Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program
defences.description: A penetration testing programme appropriate to the enterprise — scope, frequency, limitations, remediation requirements.

defences.title: 18.2 Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests
defences.description: External penetration tests at least annually, including enterprise and environmental reconnaissance.

defences.title: 18.3 Remediate Penetration Test Findings
defences.description: Penetration test findings are remediated according to the remediation policy.

defences.title: 18.4 Validate Security Measures
defences.description: Security measures are validated after each penetration test, and rulesets and capabilities adjusted to detect the techniques used.

defences.title: 18.5 Perform Periodic Internal Penetration Tests
defences.description: Internal penetration tests at least annually, clear box or opaque box.

defences.title: Cyber insurance (risk transfer)
defences.description: A cyber policy covering incident response, restoration, business interruption and liability. Insurers increasingly require IG1-level safeguards — MFA, backups, patching — before they will cover ransomware.
